source.title: Geospatial Mechanistic Interpretability of Large Language Models
source.authors: S. De Sabbata; Stefano Mizzaro; Kevin Roitero

record.tranche_reason: The study uses spatial autocorrelation and sparse autoencoders, rather than the original neuron-pole audit, and reports results about neuron polysemanticity and the interpretability of extracted features.
record.gate_note: The study reports spatial-autocorrelation results for neurons and sparse-autoencoder features, including an explicit interpretation of the neurons as polysemantic. These results do not count main jobs per neuron pole. Results from cited studies and values used to select the SAE configuration are not recorded as findings.
record.test_reason: No version is tested. The 'neurons' studied are the 4,096 post-attention normalised residual-stream activations of Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, mean-pooled over placename prompts, not MLP neuron poles. The only measure is spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I). It cannot count how many jobs a unit has or what share of units are interpretable. The polysemanticity claim rests on four hand-picked examples (Figure 2), not an audit. The SAE results describe the quality of a trained replacement decomposition on geographic inputs, not the share of interpretable neurons under better tools or architectures. These are related but different constructs, so they are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors say geographic information appears distributed across polysemantic neurons, consistent with superposition, and that SAEs plus spatial analysis yield clearer, more monosemantic geospatial features. They call the results preliminary and say the decomposition needs improvement.
record.recipe_differences: Uses spatial autocorrelation on placename activations and a TopK SAE trained on condensed layer-15 activations; it does not perform a neuron-pole job audit or test explanations on held-out activating examples.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors note that different extracted activations, SAE bottleneck size, sparsity method, or training choices may provide different insights; they report training four k settings and selecting k = 2,048 based on final training loss.

fits_no_version.finding: In Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, 1,841 of 12,288 post-attention residual dimensions (layers 7/15/31, mean-pooled over placename prompts) show significant spatial autocorrelation. Example dimensions show high values for several distinct regions, which the authors call polysemantic.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual-stream dimensions of a 7B LLM, probed with placename prompts, carry spatially autocorrelated geographic signal, and individual dimensions appear to mix several regions.

fits_no_version.finding: A TopK SAE (32,768 features, k=2,048) on layer-15 pooled activations yields 67 features (0.2%) with significant spatial autocorrelation, some appearing monosemantic (southern Italy, 'urban'). 99.53% of its features are always zero on these inputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features trained on geographic prompt activations can isolate spatially coherent geographic concepts, but with a small-data SAE most features are dead.

record.problems: The authors call the experiments preliminary. The SAE was trained on the whole dataset because generalisation was not sought; 99.53% of its features always produced zero for the placenames, and only 67 features met the spatial-autocorrelation criterion. Spatial autocorrelation is not a direct measure of semantic job count, and the study tests one model and one geospatial setting.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B, no neuron-pole audit, no shares for one job, two related jobs or not understood.
No cross-model or scale comparison and no share estimates. The units are residual dimensions of one 7B model.
No InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron re-examination; recursive generalization is not tested.
No comparison of tools or architectures on the share of interpretable neurons; no vision models; the 5% to 99% estimates are not tested.
No test of explanations against held-out firing.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked R1 to V1 and R2/R3 to V4 and gave labels. These links fail the 'same behaviour, same kind of unit' test. The units are residual-stream dimensions, not MLP neurons. No job counting or interpretable-share estimate is made. The polysemanticity evidence is anecdotal, from 4 examples, and partly driven by region names included in the prompts. The study's framing assumes superposition rather than testing it against the essay's account.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit Qwen3-32B, distinguish positive and negative neuron poles, or estimate the shares with one job, two related jobs, or not-yet-understood jobs.
No comparison across models or scales, and no dense-versus-MoE or trillion-parameter analysis.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car example or test of recursive generalization.

Tests one SAE configuration on one model and a geospatial interpretability measure only; does not test architecture or regularization effects, InceptionV1-sized vision models, or the stated 5%-to-99% estimates.
No attribution graphs or test of whether neurons alone reconstruct model behavior.
Does not test explanations against new activating examples or measure prediction of neuron firing.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2
rows.operation_detail: Calculated spatial autocorrelation for condensed neuron activations across layers 7, 15, and 31.
rows.measure: Number and share of neurons with significant spatial autocorrelation; authors also describe the high-autocorrelation neurons as polysemantic.
rows.value: 1,841 (14.98%) neurons across the three layers displayed significant autocorrelation. The authors state that neurons with high spatial autocorrelation did not seem monosemantic; examples showed high values for multiple areas or concepts.
rows.note: The reported percentage is the share meeting the spatial-autocorrelation criterion, not the share of neuron poles with one or more jobs. The text describes examples at layers 7, 15, and 31, including different patterns within a layer; it does not give a comprehensive job count.
rows.check: The units are residual-stream dimensions (post-attention norm, before the MLP), mean-pooled across tokens, not MLP neuron poles. 1,841 (14.98% of 12,288 dimensions across 3 layers) is the count passing the spatial-autocorrelation criterion, not a job-count share. The 'polysemantic' reading comes from 4 example dimensions, and several of their 'multiple areas' are prompt-named regions (New York, Northern Ireland). The measure cannot show the V1/V2 one-job share.

rows.subject: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2
rows.operation_detail: Applied spatial autocorrelation to features from an SAE trained on layer-15 condensed activations.

conditions.value: 4,096 inputs expanded to 32,768 features; TopK with ReLU, k = 2,048; 300 epochs
UK, Italy, and four US states

rows.measure: Number and share of SAE features with significant spatial autocorrelation.
rows.value: 67 of 32,768 features (0.2%) displayed significant spatial autocorrelation.
rows.note: The authors describe the extracted features as displaying clearer spatially coherent patterns, but spatial autocorrelation is a geospatial measure, not a general measure of feature interpretability or a direct count of interpretable neurons.
rows.check: This is the share of SAE features (a trained replacement basis) meeting a geospatial autocorrelation criterion on one dataset. It does not measure the share of interpretable neurons, or a rise in that share with better tools or modern architectures (V4). The SAE k value was chosen on training loss, and the SAE was trained on the same data it was evaluated on.

rows.subject: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2
rows.operation_detail: Measured whether SAE encoder features activated for any of the input placenames.

conditions.value: 32,768 features; TopK with ReLU, k = 2,048; 300 epochs
UK, Italy, and four US states

rows.measure: Share of SAE features always producing zero, and share with minimal or not significant spatial autocorrelation.
rows.value: 99.53% of features always generated a zero value for all input placenames; 0.27% displayed minimal or not significant spatial autocorrelation.
rows.note: The authors say these results indicate that further work is needed to improve the decomposition. The two reported shares describe different feature outcomes and are retained as stated.
rows.check: 99.53% always-zero features is a dead-feature/decomposition-quality statistic for this SAE, which the authors say needs improving. It says nothing about neuron interpretability shares.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
